_comment: The worked experiment for WORDING-TESTS.md, and a template for your own.
THE FAILURE UNDER TEST is one this repository's own always-on instruction file already
forbids: a deliverable written for a reader who never saw the machinery should not name the
machinery. The rule exists, it is written down, and nothing measures whether any particular
phrasing of it works. That is the gap this experiment is pointed at.
WHY A STRING COUNT AND NOT A JUDGE. The metric has to be reproducible by someone who does not
trust us, and it has to be independent of the thing being measured. Counting fixed strings is
both. A model scoring model output would put the measurement and the subject in the same
family, and the first thing a wording change would move is the judge.
THE ARMS ARE THE POINT. 'control' is not a formality -- it is step one, and the runner refuses
to compare anything if the control never exhibits the failure. 'prohibition' and 'recipe' say
the same thing in the two forms an author actually chooses between: forbid the bad output, or
describe the good one. They are not equivalent and this is how you find out.
The fixture is a real work log from this repository, kept deliberately dense with names.
_control_contamination_note: THE TASK LINE IS BARE ON PURPOSE, and the first version of it was not.
It originally read '...for a programme officer who funds this team and has never opened the
repository'. Measured 2026-08-17: the control scored zero on every one of seven reps, and the
runner refused to go further. That audience clause IS the instruction under test, phrased as
task framing, so the control arm already carried the guidance the other arms were supposed to
add -- and every arm would have tied at the floor while looking like agreement.
This is the failure mode the control-first rule exists to catch, and it caught its own
experiment before it caught anything else. If you copy this file, read your task line for
fixture: Added Test-ScriptQuality.ps1, a five-check gate over every .ps1 the pack ships, with its registry at practice-gate/script-quality.json. Wired a pinned PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 install plus the gate into build-and-verify.yml, and the four module-free checks into the portable verify.yml so Invoke-LocalCI picks them up. Found that eight of ten scripts were UTF-8 with no BOM, that wt.ps1 uses null-coalescing without a #requires guard, and that five callers read a failed git status as clean. Ran the gate with -Analyzer and recorded 29 findings against the registry.

arms.name: prohibition
arms.guidance: Do not mention any tool, script, file, flag or product name.

arms.name: recipe
arms.guidance: Refer to each step by what it achieved, in the words someone who has never seen the machinery would use.
